o: We classify each submission date as weekend (Saturday/Sunday) or working day and output two counts. In the sample, dates 2022-06-18/19 fall on Sat/Sun giving weekend_cnt = 3, the rest give working_cnt = 3. MySQL's DAYOFWEEK returns 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday, so weekend means DAYOFWEEK IN (1, 7).
k: DAYOFWEEK(): 1 = Sunday, 7 = Saturday — weekend test is IN (1, 7).
Conditional aggregation (SUM(CASE WHEN ...)) produces both counts in a single pass.

a.i: Aggregate over the whole table with two conditional sums — one counting weekend days, one counting the complement. No GROUP BY is needed since we want a single row.
s: Select SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(submit_date) IN (1,7) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as weekend_cnt.
Select the complementary sum as working_cnt.

c.python:
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(submit_date) IN (1, 7) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS weekend_cnt,
  SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(submit_date) NOT IN (1, 7) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS working_cnt
FROM Tasks;

w: Alternative dialect notes: use WEEKDAY() (5 = Sat, 6 = Sun) in MySQL, or TO_CHAR(date, 'DY') / EXTRACT(DOW) elsewhere. Pitfall: confusing DAYOFWEEK (Sunday-first) with WEEKDAY (Monday-first) shifts the weekend test by two days. Follow-up: group counts per assignee — add GROUP BY assignee_id.
